We are seeking a Full Stack Software Engineer to join a GenAI team working on foundational AI models. description_preview:
About Glasslake
Glasslake is building the operating system for SAP delivery — the infrastructure layer underneath the most complex and expensive IT projects companies run. SAP implementations move billions of dollars and thousands of consultants, but the knowledge generated in these projects is never captured: it lives in people's heads, disappears when the project ends, and gets rebuilt from scratch on every new engagement.
Glasslake solves this with an agentic orchestration platform that coordinates every phase of SAP transformation, capturing decisions, tests, and context as a byproduct of work already underway — building an organizational memory that accumulates across projects instead of resetting.
We're a team based in San Francisco and São Paulo, moving fast and already deployed with some of the largest SAP integrators in the world, including delaware Consulting, KPMG, and NTT Data. The team comes from Stanford, McKinsey, Meta, Two Sigma, Robinhood, Microsoft, and NASA.
The Opportunity
You'll build the interfaces consultants and enterprise teams use to navigate complex implementations and work with AI agents. These workflows involve substantial information, interconnected decisions, and work that unfolds over time. Your job is to make that complexity understandable and manageable through thoughtful, responsive software.
You'll work closely with design and other engineers, and talk directly to customers to understand where they're encountering friction. You'll help shape what we build, prototype alternatives, ship improvements, and follow through on how they perform in production.
Your primary focus will be the frontend: both the experiences users interact with and the foundations that help our team build them well. You'll have room to make consequential technical decisions and the responsibility to keep them practical — using AI-assisted development tools to explore and iterate, while applying your own judgment to the quality and simplicity of what we ship.
What You'll Do
Own product outcomes.
Take ambiguous problems from customer conversations through implementation, deployment, and iteration.
Build the core interfaces.
Ship the experiences consultants and enterprise teams use to navigate complex implementations and work with AI agents.
Reason from UX back into implementation.
Decide which interactions need to feel instantaneous, how state and data should flow, and when a problem calls for a better component, a different loading strategy, or a change to an API.
Design for real usage.
Think through loading, empty, error, and recovery states; collaborate closely with design; treat accessibility as part of a complete experience.
Build durable foundations.
Recognize reusable interaction patterns, design clear component APIs, and use composition and shared primitives to keep the product consistent as it grows.
Make the product feel fast.
Reason about rendering, network requests, caching, prefetching, and feedback during longer operations — and measure whether changes actually help.
Work across boundaries.
Reason about APIs, data models, and backend behavior when they affect the frontend, and make pragmatic build-vs-use calls.
Raise the team's bar.
Work independently, communicate decisions clearly, and improve the experience of engineers building alongside you — including how the team uses AI-assisted workflows.
What We're Looking For
Deep frontend fundamentals.
You've shipped and maintained complex interactive applications, and understand JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML and CSS, browser behavior, rendering, state management, and asynchronous data flow.
Strong UX judgment.
You think in terms of how people will actually use a feature, not just whether it works.
Evidence-driven.
You combine customer feedback with analytics, performance monitoring, and session replay to identify friction and evaluate the impact of changes.
Ownership.
You ask questions, challenge assumptions, and care whether what you shipped actually helped, not just whether it shipped.
Pragmatism.
You know when to use an existing library, when custom implementation is worthwhile, and how to balance immediate delivery with longer-term maintainability.
Curiosity and judgment.
Above all, you understand problems deeply, explore possible solutions, and make thoughtful trade-offs between user experience, engineering quality, speed, and complexity.
Nice to have
Experience building interfaces for AI-powered products, including workflows where users review, guide, or approve agent actions.
Experience evolving a component library or design system while continuing to ship product features.
Experience on a small team where you helped shape product and design decisions alongside engineering.
Familiarity with complex enterprise workflows or ecosystems such as SAP, Salesforce, ERP, or CRM.
Why Join Glasslake Now
Shape the interfaces for a product with proven traction inside the largest SAP integrators in the world — delaware Consulting, KPMG, and NTT Data — in a category being defined right now.
Own consequential technical decisions on a small, senior team, with a short line between an idea and it being in production.
Build the frontend foundations for a company with a team from Stanford, Meta, Two Sigma, Microsoft, and NASA.
Work at the center of an emerging category: interfaces where humans and AI agents collaborate on high-stakes, high-complexity work.

About Exus Renewables North America
Exus Renewables North America is a leading independent developer and operator of utility-scale renewable energy projects, dedicated to advancing clean energy solutions across the United States. With offices in Pittsburgh, New York, and Albuquerque, and over 100 employees in the US, Exus NA focuses on developing, repowering, and managing renewable energy assets, contributing to the nation's decarbonization efforts and driving sustainable growth in the U.S. renewable energy sector.
The
Project Engineer
will routinely meet with the Project Managers, Site Managers, Director of Construction, and the Head of Construction while performing the duties associated with this position. The Project Engineer will be assigned to one or more of the projects currently under contract. The Project Engineer will assist the Head of Construction with assigned tasks from time to time.
This role is open to December 2026 recent engineering graduates!
Essential Responsibilities
The Project Engineer works continuously toward successful project completion by assisting the Director of Construction and the Site Managers in monitoring projects in a manner consistent with the intent of the contract requirements, specifications, and metrics appropriate to the project.
Perform safety audits and interact with contractors and subcontractors to ensure the site is working safely and a positive safety culture is implemented at the site.
Take the lead in quickly resolving issues which can impact the project’s schedule, quality, and budget for areas that have been assigned to the Project Engineer.
Auditing project files and drawings to ensure that project teams maintain documents in an orderly fashion and are utilizing the latest revisions of documents on the project sites.
Obtaining submittals, transmittals, and requests for information (RFIs) from Vendors and Contractors and routing or answering in a timely manner to support the project schedules.
Reviewing submittals, transmittals, RFIs and schedules for accuracy and adherence to project requirements.
Performing appropriate follow up on submittals, transmittals, and RFIs for additional information and action items.
Track project deliverables (such as schedule updates, lien waivers, and work plans) to ensure documents are submitted timely and accurately.
Perform field productivity audits tracking manpower, equipment, cycle times, and units installed.
Assisting the project teams in documenting issues that could impact EXUS’ interests.
Ability to read drawings (all disciplines), understand quality control requirements, and assess Project Schedules for risks and opportunities.
Support independent engineer documentation process/review of project documentation (does deep dive on everything from the job, tracks down missing documentation, answering questions, submitting to engineers, etc.)
Education And Experience Requirements
Bachelors in civil or electrical engineering, or construction management.
1+ years of experience in a position of responsibility with a construction or engineering firm, internships included.
Prior experience assisting on projects from groundbreaking to project turnover highly preferred.
Prior experience utilizing Word, Excel, Primavera, and select Project Management software highly preferred.
Travel as required, up to 75% to sites beyond the corporate office to project sites.
Be assigned to a project site with an undetermined duration, if project metrics dictate additional management onsite.

Current HHMI Employees, click here to apply via your Workday account.
TLDR:
Build AI methods for 3D particle detection and structural analysis in cryo-electron tomography data, applied to chromatin organization and synaptic molecular targets.
Please include a cover letter with your application. Describe a deep learning project you have executed, ideally involving 3D image analysis, inverse problems, or physics-informed modeling. Cryo-EM/ET and computational structural biology projects are especially relevant. Discuss results, limitations, and challenges encountered. If the project was collaborative, describe your specific contributions. Include links to relevant code repositories and your GitHub/Gitlab profile, personal website, or similar evidence.
About the role:
AI@HHMI:
HHMI is investing $500 million over the next 10 years to support AI-driven projects and to embed AI systems throughout every stage of the scientific process in labs across HHMI. This role is part of the AI+CryoET project within AI@HHMI, a multi-institutional project at the intersection of cryo-electron tomography (cryoET), molecular dynamics simulation, and machine learning. The project aims to develop AI methods for mesoscale structural biology, understanding how cellular macromolecules organize into higher-order structures. You will work in a team at Janelia, with experimental and computational collaborators across the Rosen lab (UT Southwestern Medical Center/HHMI), Gouaux lab (Oregon Health and Science University/HHMI), Collepardo-Guevara lab (University of Cambridge), and Villa lab (UC San Diego/HHMI).
You will develop machine learning methods for particle detection, localization, and structural analysis in cryoET data, with two interconnected aims: (1) detecting gold nanoparticle (AuNP) probes to improve reconstruction quality and identify molecular targets; (2) identifying the arrangement and connectivity of nucleosomes in chromatin that give rise to chromosome structure in cell nuclei and biochemical reconstitutions. This involves developing supervised and self-supervised AI models based on simulated as well as annotated experimental cryoET data, informed by molecular dynamics simulations of relevant biological structures. Success in this role requires close collaboration with cryoET experts, structural biologists, and computer scientists to ensure models work in challenging real-world scenarios of a biologically not yet fully understood system.
What we provide:
A competitive compensation package with comprehensive health and welfare benefits.
A supportive team environment that promotes collaboration and knowledge sharing.
Access to world-class computational infrastructure, GPU-based computing environments, and unique high-quality cryoET datasets.
The opportunity to work directly with leading structural biologists, cryoET experimentalists, and molecular dynamics experts on a highly interdisciplinary project.
The opportunity to engage with world-class researchers, software engineers, and AI/ML experts, contribute to impactful science, and be part of a dynamic community committed to advancing humanity's understanding of fundamental scientific questions.
Amenities that enhance work-life balance, such as on-site childcare, free gyms, available on-campus housing, social and dining spaces, and convenient shuttle bus service to Janelia from the Washington, D.C. metro area.
Opportunity to partner with frontier AI labs on scientific applications of AI. See https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-partners-with-allen-institute-and-howard-hughes-medical-institute
What you'll do:
Develop and evaluate deep learning models for detecting and localizing gold nanoparticles and macromolecular particles (e.g., nucleosomes, synaptic receptors) in cryoET data, and for identification of nucleosome arrangement and connectivity in chromatin.
Develop methods to leverage gold nanoparticle detections to improve tomogram reconstruction, addressing challenges in tilt-series alignment, deformations, and low signal-to-noise conditions.
Design and execute rigorous AI model training and evaluation pipelines, including proper handling of missing wedge artifacts, CTF effects, and sim-to-real transfer from MD-derived synthetic training data.
Identify where additional human annotation and proofreading will be most helpful and design and guide annotation efforts.
Contribute to scientific publications, present findings at conferences, and maintain a well-documented codebase enabling seamless reproduction and extension of results.
Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams across multiple institutions.
What you bring:
Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Computational Chemistry, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
3+ years training and evaluating deep learning models, particularly on 3D or volumetric image data. Experience with detection, segmentation, or inverse problems in imaging is strongly preferred.
Strong Python skills, and proficiency in PyTorch and/or JAX. Ability to reason about neural network behavior from first principles: how architectural choices, regularization, and training procedures affect model behavior.

Design verification mechanisms that can automatically verify a solution to a software engineering task.

description_preview:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Member of Technical Staff based in the United States.
The Member of Technical Staff will design, build, and deploy full-stack software solutions that transform healthcare practice operations through AI-powered automation. You will own features end to end, from identifying real-world problems with clinicians and operational teams to delivering reliable solutions in production. Working across the entire technology stack, you will develop intelligent agents and workflows that streamline insurance verification, patient intake, claims processing, and clinical documentation. You will combine strong software engineering skills with hands-on experience using AI coding agents to accelerate development and improve engineering productivity. This role offers significant autonomy, a flat engineering structure, and the opportunity to shape products used by clinicians, patients, and healthcare operations teams. You will also help ensure that sensitive healthcare information is handled securely while building scalable technology for a growing healthcare platform.
Accountabilities
In this role, you will take ownership of technical projects from problem definition through implementation, deployment, and ongoing optimization, collaborating closely with clinical and operational stakeholders.
Design and develop AI agents and automated workflows for healthcare operations, including insurance benefits verification, prior authorizations, patient intake, claims processing, and clinical documentation.
Build and maintain web and mobile features for clinicians, patients, families, and internal operations teams.
Translate ambiguous business and clinical challenges into clear specifications, technical solutions, and initial product releases.
Design and implement backend services, data models, APIs, and supporting infrastructure using infrastructure-as-code practices.
Own services throughout their lifecycle, including deployment, production monitoring, troubleshooting, and incident response.
Develop evaluations for AI-powered features, monitor model performance, and track operational metrics to ensure reliable workflow outcomes.
Protect sensitive health information through least-privilege access controls, secure data handling, logging restrictions, and auditable changes.
Build and maintain engineering tools that support AI-assisted development, including skills, plugins, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, and automated code-review bots.
Use AI coding agents to accelerate implementation, manage parallel development tasks, and review generated code for correctness, security, and maintainability.
Contribute across the full technology platform, working with frontend, backend, data, and infrastructure components in an established codebase.
Collaborate with distributed teammates through clear technical specifications, pull requests, tickets, and written documentation.
Requirements
The ideal candidate is a product-minded software engineer who combines full-stack expertise with practical AI development experience, strong ownership, and the ability to deliver reliable production systems in a fast-moving environment.
At least 3 years of experience building and shipping production software.
Demonstrated ability to own products or features end to end, from an unclear initial problem through implementation and delivery of systems that users rely on.
Strong full-stack development skills in Python and TypeScript, with experience across frontend applications, backend services, databases, and cloud infrastructure.
Comfort working within a large, established codebase and navigating existing architectural and technical constraints.
Hands-on experience developing applications with large language models (LLMs), including tool use, agent orchestration, structured outputs, retrieval, and evaluation frameworks such as LangGraph or comparable agent SDKs.
Daily experience using AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor, including configuring project instructions, skills, MCP servers, hooks, and subagents; coordinating parallel tasks; and carefully reviewing generated code.
Strong product judgment and the ability to make sound user interface decisions independently using an existing component library.
High ownership and initiative, with the ability to investigate problems, find relevant context, remove blockers, and ask focused questions when needed.
Clear written communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across time zones in a distributed engineering team.
A strong commitment to software quality, security, reliability, and responsible handling of sensitive information.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in healthcare or another regulated industry, including HIPAA requirements, payer and claims workflows, electronic health record (EHR) integrations, or HL7/FHIR standards.
Experience with Temporal or another durable workflow orchestration engine.
Experience building mobile applications with React Native.
Experience running LLM evaluations or safety checks on model outputs in production.
Experience developing custom agent harnesses, MCP servers, or plugins for AI coding tools.
Contributions to open-source projects, side projects, or internal tools used by other people.
Candidates who meet most of the requirements and are excited about the role are encouraged to apply, even if they do not satisfy every preferred qualification.
Benefits
Remote work: Remote position, with the listed locations including Uruguay, Bangalore, India, and remote India. The role's stated locations do not include the United States, so applicants should confirm geographic eligibility.
Technical ownership: Opportunity to own features and services across the full software development lifecycle.
AI innovation: Daily use of modern AI coding agents and opportunities to build AI-powered healthcare workflows.

GDIT is seeking a Cloud Data Engineer (Azure) to support the Indian Health Service Four Directions Data Warehouse (IHS 4DW) project.
IHS, an agency within the Department of Health and Human Services, is the principal federal health care provider and health advocate for American Indian and Alaska Native (AI/AN) people. This role supports a mission-critical modernization effort: retiring the Resource and Patient Management System (RPMS) and moving to a new electronic health record (EHR) system.
At GDIT, people are our differentiator. As a Cloud Data Engineer, you’ll help deliver cutting-edge cloud and data solutions that directly support improved healthcare outcomes while growing your career in a collaborative, mission-driven environment.
HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT
Lead the modernization of IHS health records by establishing a central repository for clinical data and longitudinal patient records.
Design and implement Azure data pipelines to consolidate clinical data from 200+ healthcare facilities into an enterprise analytics environment.
Develop automated ETL processes for high-volume JSON/HL7 FHIR data using Azure Data Factory and Azure Data Lake.
Create and optimize PySpark processes for large-scale healthcare data transformation and enrichment.
Build and maintain enterprise data models to standardize clinical information across facilities and data sources.
Implement monitoring and alerting solutions to ensure data quality, reliability, and pipeline performance.
Collaborate with architects, data engineers, and stakeholders to define cloud data architecture and integration patterns.
Provide technical leadership on Azure cloud and data engineering best practices.
WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED
Technical training, certification(s), or degree and 3+ years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Ability to serve as a lead big data engineer on database migration and Azure-based data pipeline initiatives.
Extensive experience with Azure data services, including:
Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2
Azure Synapse Analytics
Azure Data Factory
Azure Monitor
Spark clusters (e.g., Synapse Spark, Databricks, or HDInsight)
Proficiency in SQL and data modeling for enterprise-scale databases and analytics environments.
Strong programming skills in Python (including PySpark) and .NET for large-scale data processing and integration.
Experience developing Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Bicep, ARM templates, Terraform) and RESTful APIs in Azure.
Track record of implementing CI/CD pipelines and DevOps practices for data-oriented solutions.
NICE TO HAVE
Relevant Azure certifications such as:
Azure Data Engineer Associate (DP-203)
Azure Database Administrator Associate (DP-300)
Azure Solutions Architect Expert (AZ-305)
Experience in healthcare data systems and clinical data workflows.
Advanced Power BI data visualization and semantic model development skills.
Experience with HL7 FHIR implementation and healthcare data standards.
Experience with Agile methodologies and technical team leadership or mentorship.
Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field.

There are two positions available that may be filled at either the Associate Engineer (entry level) or Engineer level (2+ years), commensurate with the successful candidate’s experience, education, knowledge, skills, and abilities. These positions will be within the Electric Transmission Quality Assurance (ETQA) group and will primarily support the Inverter-Based Resource (IBR) Site Inspection and Power Quality programs.
The successful candidates will perform and support field inspections, configuration verification, power quality monitoring, data collection, and documentation activities associated with transmission-connected IBR facilities and other facilities impacting the transmission system. Responsibilities will include comparing installed equipment, settings, and configurations against applicable engineering documentation and requirements; identifying and documenting discrepancies; supporting pre-generation and post-generation power quality monitoring activities; reviewing field and monitoring data for completeness; preparing inspection and monitoring records; and coordinating with engineering, field, operations, project, and other stakeholder organizations to support resolution of identified issues.
